li.title: Three Hundred Years
li.text:
The world ended and then it did not. That is the short version, and most people out here have never heard a longer one.

A thousand years of ash came down on an empire run by a man who had made himself a god, and it stopped inside a single day. The histories say two people died holding the pieces apart long enough for a third to catch them, and that the third is still holding them, and answers to Harmony. The Ministry is gone. The Lord Ruler is a thing schoolchildren argue about. Ash is a word for something that used to fall.

Three hundred years is long enough to rebuild, and long enough to forget you were rebuilding. Elendel has banks and broadsheets and a governor, and railroads pushing west. Past the last of them the law is whoever rode out to enforce it and how long they intend to stay.

This is the Roughs. Harmony is real, He is listening, and He is a very long way away.

li.title: The Roughs Have Teeth
li.text: Two claim camps burned this month and a rail crew walked back forty miles because their handcar did not. Whoever is doing it is organised, and getting bolder about being seen.\n\nThey are riding this way. There is a gang out there now with a name and a territory, and the colony is inside it.

li.title: The Vanishers
li.text: An entire rail shipment - cargo, passengers, rolling stock - gone between one station and the next. No wreckage and no bodies, which is not how robbery works.\n\nThey are Metalborn, they are funded, and they are not going to stay on the rail line. The next thing that comes at the colony will be better armed than the last.

li.title: Miles Hundredlives
li.text:
The man running the Vanishers used to be a lawman. Twenty years in the Roughs, a good one, and somewhere in there he decided the law was a thing the Basin used on people like him and stopped pretending otherwise.

They call him Hundredlives because that is roughly how many times somebody has watched him die. He heals. Shoot him and the hole closes; the only thing that has ever worked is doing it faster than he can mend.

He is coming here, and he is not in a hurry, because he has never had a reason to be.

li.title: He Got Back Up
li.text:
Somebody counted the hits. Somebody else confirmed the count. It did not matter.

He walked out of the treeline three days later with the same coat and the same unhurried expression, and the people who had watched him go down are having difficulty with it in a way that is starting to affect how they hold a rifle.

He is not going to stop coming. The only question is what runs out first.

li.title: They're Coming
li.text:
The third time took. Whatever he had stored ran out somewhere in the middle of it, and the wound stayed a wound, and he seemed almost interested in that.

He was still talking at the end. Not pleading - he had never done that - but explaining, in the tone of a man laying out the part everyone else has missed. He said they were coming. He said he had only ever been early.

He did not say who, and there was not time to make him. The Vanishers scatter without him. Whatever he was working for does not.
